coverage.risk: An earlier successful compiler child can survive later failure or scratch deletion.
coverage.assessment: PASS: three orderings are jobs2 a-success/b-failure in one batch, jobs1 a-success/b-failure across batches, and jobs2 a-success/c-failure across batches. AFTER_SUCCESS waits for the a.c end event before the later failure. Four failure/success subcases require nonempty child-state observations at the private rm observer, absence or zombie state for every recorded child, scratch removal and appropriate return/link behavior. All pass on macOS and pinned Linux.

coverage.risk: A successful invocation or signal after a successful driver could forget its child.
coverage.assessment: PASS: a successful serial build leaves an ELF and stops the child before scratch deletion. Jobs1 and jobs2 HUP/INT/TERM subcases wait for the later hanging compiler child, require the earlier child already stopped, send the signal, require 128+signal return, both children stopped before deletion, no ELF and no scratch.

coverage.risk: Regression fixtures could pass the original faulty source or fail for setup errors.
coverage.assessment: PASS: negative runner reads exact parent 78c5296 source into a private scratch root and requires ten failures with no errors. Logs contain four child-active-at-scratch assertions and six earlier-child-active-before-signal assertions on each platform. The six original-source signal subcases fail at the pre-signal stopped-child check, so those negative controls do not themselves prove original signal delivery. Repaired passing subcases do send and verify each signal. Expected unittest failure traces are followed by explicit PASS and wrapper rc0.

coverage.risk: New cleanup could break existing orchestration.
coverage.assessment: PASS: seven saved methods cover jobs1/2/4 exact peak bounds, serial mode, ordered diagnostic streams and link objects, LTO flag presence, invalid job counts, stale-success removal, failed-driver child cleanup and interruption joining direct drivers and children. Exact candidate and fixture hashes match both saved platform records.

coverage.risk: Evidence reuse could omit previously accepted Quickcheck behavior.
coverage.assessment: PASS: all source outside the two controller files is byte-identical to original candidate30c567d. Six unaffected suite logs and the two independent adversarial command logs match their recorded hashes. Preserve conservative unknown/mixed/empty/firmware/error and rename/deletion handling; selected real PASS reports and partial-report rejection; unreadable source failure; current rules and explicit STE handling; host-build/uploader dependencies; preference history guards; fixed regression and parent negative controls.

coverage.risk: Fixture cleanup could signal unrelated processes or conceal the defect.
coverage.assessment: PASS by source review: monitor reads private CHILDREN state before execing real rm. Recorded child PIDs belong to fake compilers in temporary roots. Cleanup runs after assertions or in finally and signals only those recorded PIDs; no broad process search or kill command exists. It does not change the observed failure into a pass.

failure_dispositions.failure: The first Linux negative-control attempt could not read Git due to Docker root versus host repository ownership.
failure_dispositions.repair: Use git -c safe.directory=<this exact lane> only on the scratch old-source read. No global settings changed. One bounded retry reran only the failed negative control; the suite PASS was reused.

failure_dispositions.failure: The initial staged whitespace check reported unittest progress-line spaces in raw negative-control logs. Source-only whitespace and shell syntax checks passed.
failure_dispositions.repair: Normalise trailing whitespace in saved test logs without changing assertions or outcomes. Retain original raw-output SHA-256 alongside normalised log SHA-256; verify all updated identities.

failure_dispositions.failure: The first independent evidence verifier counted assertion source lines as well as actual assertion failures in negative-control traces.
failure_dispositions.repair: Restrict counting to lines that begin AssertionError. No source, fixture, or saved execution result changed.

limits: This independent review reused matching macOS and pinned Linux executions; no controller suite or Quickcheck suite was repeated solely for stage or commit changes. No concrete unresolved coverage doubt required a new scratch behavior probe.

Normalised saved log hashes were independently verified. The pre-normalisation raw-output digests remain saved provenance metadata; the raw streams are not retained here for recomputation. Normalisation strips trailing whitespace only, and observed assertions and outcomes remain intact.
The seven original suite records remain; the old controller fixture result is superseded by the current seven-method macOS/Linux runs.

The saved real controller result/log identity is preserved; independent investigation and root own full image/environment/source-equivalence acceptance. This reviewer did not rehash proprietary dependencies or run a real controller, baseline or application build.
No source changes, runner registration, release/full gate, install, device check, external push, proprietary bundle or firmware integration.
Direct fixture runner registration remains with the runner/combination owner. Fixed-tree devbug reuse remains deferred.
